papers.summary:
-  We classified 237 files: 126 data, 69 code, 36 documentation, 3 output, 3 unknown.
-  We found 33 tabular data files and extracted 276 columns from 28 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  5 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (identity_check_STOPPED_credit_exhausted.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; fetch_time_parse50.txt: the file has no data rows or columns; fetch_time_parse_other.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; fetch_time.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; revision_2026-11_outputs.zip/revision_2026-11/data/raw/osf_fa42s/th45d_download/fa42s_validation_log.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: identity_check_STOPPED_credit_exhausted.txt, fetch_time_parse50.txt, fetch_time_parse_other.txt, fetch_time.txt, revision_2026-11_outputs.zip/revision_2026-11/data/raw/osf_fa42s/th45d_download/fa42s_validation_log.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 276 columns; 6 columns have at least one potential issue (5 columns with inconsistent category casing; 1 column with no observed values (entirely empty)).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 2210 files: 582 data, 7 code, 1621 materials.
-  We found 582 tabular data files and extracted 1402 columns from 163 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 23 study groups (ex1, ex10, ex11, ex12, ex13, ex14, ex15, ex16, ex17, ex18, ex2, ex20, ex21, ex22, ex23, ex24, ex25, ex26, ex3, ex4, ex5, ex6, ex7).
-  419 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1402 columns; 13 columns have at least one potential issue (13 columns with numeric values stored as text).

papers.title: Presaccadic Attention in Dynamic Scenes: Evidence from Hazard Localization in Road Videos
papers.summary:
-  We classified 2832 files: 78 data, 2 code, 3 documentation, 2749 materials.
-  We found 30 tabular data files and extracted 779 columns from 30 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 8 study groups (ex03, ex04, ex05, ex06, ex07, ex09, ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  Repository https://osf.io/8a6bk exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 15 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more. We ran automated data-quality checks on 779 columns; 103 columns have at least one potential issue (46 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 24 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 24 columns whose values look like personal information; 24 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 8 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic column for Age.

papers.title: I Remember That Question: Using Eye Tracking to See How Prequestions Shape Reading
papers.summary:
-  We classified 578 files: 452 data, 25 code, 44 documentation, 55 materials, 1 output, 1 unknown.
-  We found 408 tabular data files and extracted 11757 columns from 347 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, pilot1), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (r_package_versions.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: r_package_versions.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 11757 columns; 730 columns have at least one potential issue (365 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 339 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 170 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 25 columns with inconsistent category casing; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 3 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Memory Overlap Shapes General and Specific Memory Differently in Adolescents and Adults
papers.summary:
-  We classified 347 files: 76 data, 57 code, 8 documentation, 206 materials.
-  We found 1 tabular data file and extracted 3 columns from 1 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 3 columns and found no issues. We detected demographic column for Age. 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

findings.label: Sheet1
findings.detail: 4 merged ranges (A17:B17, A25:B25, A36:B36, A41:B41) break the rectangular grid.

papers.title: LifeDive: Cross-kingdom phenotype estimates for 35,856 species
papers.summary:
-  We classified 27 files: 16 data, 6 code, 5 documentation.
-  We found 16 tabular data files and extracted 850 columns from 16 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 850 columns; 521 columns have at least one potential issue (521 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 3 columns that look like geographic coordinates). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

papers.title: From the app to the lexicon: Neurocognitive markers of word integration in a second language
papers.summary:
-  We classified 85 files: 74 data, 4 code, 7 documentation.
-  We found 29 tabular data files and extracted 5666 columns from 29 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 5666 columns; 1735 columns have at least one potential issue (1403 columns with numeric values stored as text; 331 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic column for Age. 24 of 26 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 371 files: 260 data, 21 code, 7 documentation, 83 materials.
-  We found 248 tabular data files and extracted 176 columns from 8 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  225 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/HU6VM exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 149 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more.
-  14 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: brmDD1dp.RData, brmDD4dp.RData, brmDD5dp.RData, brmDD3dp.RData, brmDD6dp.RData, brmDD7dp.RData, brmDD8dp.RData, brmDD9dp.RData, brmDD10dp.RData, brmDD11dp.RData, brmDD12dp.RData, brmDD13dp.RData, brmDD14dp.RData, brmDD15dp.RData.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (TRDD_Rating.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: TRDD_Rating.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 176 columns; 6 columns have at least one potential issue (6 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 1 .csv file is separated by spaces instead of commas, so its columns could not be checked; save it as comma-separated .csv (or tab-separated .tsv): TRDD_Rating.csv.

papers.title: Designing AI-Agents with Personalities: A Psychometric Approach
papers.summary:
-  We classified 282 files: 219 data, 42 code, 9 documentation, 6 materials, 6 output.
-  We found 134 tabular data files and extracted 4107 columns from 133 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 6 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex2a, ex2b, ex3, ex4), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (elaborated_binary__deepseek__bfi_to_minimarker_binary_deepseek_temp1_loadings.csv: 50% of columns are free text and 50% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: elaborated_binary__deepseek__bfi_to_minimarker_binary_deepseek_temp1_loadings.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 4107 columns; 77 columns have at least one potential issue (37 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 20 columns with numeric values stored as text; 10 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 9 columns with inconsistent category casing; 8 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 7 columns of free text that may contain personal detail). 537 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (529 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race.

papers.title: Minds Meet Machines: The Joint Role of Trust and Intellectual Humility in AI Persuasion
papers.summary:
-  We classified 30 files: 9 data, 3 code, 10 documentation, 8 materials.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 413 columns from 7 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (S1 SOM correlations.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: S1 SOM correlations.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 413 columns; 123 columns have at least one potential issue (51 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 48 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 42 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 21 columns whose name suggests personal information; 18 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 11 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns that look like geographic coordinates). 105 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (76 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 2 files are a Qualtrics survey export (25 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review). 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Perceptual distinctiveness underlies apparent emotion-specific advantages in facial expression detection
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1823 files: 1811 data, 8 code, 1 documentation, 3 materials.
-  We found 1206 tabular data files and extracted 2768 columns from 240 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex1p, ex2, ex2p), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  966 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy. We ran automated data-quality checks on 2768 columns; 392 columns have at least one potential issue (196 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 196 columns whose name suggests personal information). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

-  We classified 277 files: 88 data, 6 code, 97 documentation, 84 materials, 2 output.
-  We found 88 tabular data files and extracted 1117 columns from 84 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (analysis_environment.csv: 80% of columns are free text, not variables; Table_S9_archived_software_environment.csv: 80% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: analysis_environment.csv, Table_S9_archived_software_environment.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1117 columns; 10 columns have at least one potential issue (4 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 3 columns with numeric values stored as text; 2 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long).

papers.title: Moral Preferences for Avoiding Non-Lethal Human Injury over Property Damage in Autonomous Vehicle Accidents
papers.summary:
-  We classified 39 files: 15 data, 5 code, 1 documentation, 18 materials.
-  We found 15 tabular data files and extracted 644 columns from 15 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 644 columns; 77 columns have at least one potential issue (69 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 8 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). 15 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding. We detected demographic column for Gender.

papers.title: A mind-body disconnection? Discordance between thoughts about stress and cardiovascular stress responses
papers.summary:
-  We classified 136 files: 38 data, 22 code, 2 documentation, 64 materials, 10 output.
-  We found 38 tabular data files and extracted 3074 columns from 38 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 5 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5). We ran automated data-quality checks on 3074 columns; 140 columns have at least one potential issue (90 columns with numeric values stored as text; 34 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 10 columns whose values look like personal information; 10 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 6 of 6 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Benchmarking an automated speech recognition pipeline for Spanish-English bilingual preschoolers: Quantifying language input and output in daylong recordings.
papers.summary:
-  We classified 106 files: 26 data, 66 code, 6 documentation, 8 materials.
-  We found 25 tabular data files and extracted 1146 columns from 24 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 6 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (recording_id_map.example.csv: the file has no data rows or columns). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: recording_id_map.example.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1146 columns; 964 columns have at least one potential issue (944 columns with numeric values stored as text; 20 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 3 of 3 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Developing human-AI complementarity: Augmenting everyday decision making with Large Language Models
papers.summary:
-  We classified 10 files: 4 data, 6 materials.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 771 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3). We ran automated data-quality checks on 771 columns; 709 columns have at least one potential issue (535 columns with numeric values stored as text; 98 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 72 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 18 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing). 18 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (18 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). 4 of 4 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: From use perception to use behavior: Digitally traced smartphone use purposes and psychological well-being in daily life
papers.summary:
-  We classified 9 files: 3 data, 1 code, 5 documentation.
-  We found 3 tabular data files and extracted 1811 columns from 2 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (eMotion_sensing_feature_list.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: eMotion_sensing_feature_list.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1811 columns; 109 columns have at least one potential issue (77 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 16 columns with numeric values stored as text; 7 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 6 columns whose name suggests personal information; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns whose values look like personal information; 1 column holding an SPSS "Select Cases" filter (analyses may have used only a subset of rows)). 347 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (57 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 5 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: The Dutch Gambling Harms Question Inventory (D-GHQI-12): 	 Development, psychometric properties and test-retest reliability
papers.summary:
-  We classified 25 files: 15 data, 3 code, 6 documentation, 1 output.
-  We found 15 tabular data files and extracted 2023 columns from 15 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex5). We ran automated data-quality checks on 2023 columns; 130 columns have at least one potential issue (85 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 35 columns with inconsistent category casing; 5 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 3 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 2350 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding (1595 of them only via short-scale straightlining, which can be normal answering). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 5 of 5 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Tales of Life: Curiosity for Positive and Negative Life Stories of Culturally Close and Distant Others
papers.summary:
-  We classified 6 files: 4 data, 1 code, 1 documentation.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 1513 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 1513 columns; 1038 columns have at least one potential issue (1038 columns with numeric values stored as text). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 1 of 4 spreadsheet files has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Inequality Can Increase Stealing, Reduce Trust, and Undermine Cooperation, Even When It Is Invisible
papers.summary:
-  We classified 4899 files: 16 data, 4759 code, 74 documentation, 50 materials.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 843 columns from 6 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2). We ran automated data-quality checks on 843 columns; 124 columns have at least one potential issue (102 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 20 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 18 columns with inconsistent category casing; 8 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.

papers.title: Planning for Solitude in Retirement: A Theory of Planned Behavior Perspective on Alone Time in Older Adulthood
papers.summary:
-  We classified 8 files: 2 data, 6 documentation.
-  We found 2 tabular data files and extracted 50 columns from 2 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 50 columns; 48 columns have at least one potential issue (46 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 4 columns whose name suggests personal information; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns with numeric values stored as text). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race.

papers.title: What Is a “Blank” Mind? Testing the Meaning and Construct Validity of Mind-Blanking Reports to Thought Probes
papers.summary:
-  We classified 52 files: 41 data, 8 code, 3 documentation.
-  We found 41 tabular data files and extracted 1365 columns from 34 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1a, ex1b, ex2, ex3), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  6 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (Reject.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Reject.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1365 columns; 249 columns have at least one potential issue (154 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 40 columns whose name suggests personal information; 27 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 16 columns that look like geographic coordinates; 16 columns whose values look like personal information; 14 columns with numeric values stored as text; 8 columns with inconsistent category casing; 3 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). We detected demographic columns for Gender, Race.

papers.summary:
-  We classified 90 files: 20 data, 46 code, 4 documentation, 10 materials, 10 unknown.
-  We found 20 tabular data files and extracted 260 columns from 12 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  8 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: ?view_only=b91e790f23f046cf813e0c508fb72d06: hisims.Rdata, ?view_only=b91e790f23f046cf813e0c508fb72d06: lowsims.Rdata, ?view_only=b91e790f23f046cf813e0c508fb72d06: All code & data for the full paper/Study 2 Marketing and Consumer Psychology/hisims.Rdata, ?view_only=b91e790f23f046cf813e0c508fb72d06: All code & data for the full paper/Study 2 Marketing and Consumer Psychology/lowsims.Rdata, 25rwy: hisims.Rdata, 25rwy: lowsims.Rdata, 25rwy: All code & data for the full paper/Study 2 Marketing and Consumer Psychology/hisims.Rdata, 25rwy: All code & data for the full paper/Study 2 Marketing and Consumer Psychology/lowsims.Rdata. We ran automated data-quality checks on 260 columns; 60 columns have at least one potential issue (24 columns with numeric values stored as text; 20 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 16 columns with inconsistent category casing; 12 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 4 columns whose name suggests personal information).

papers.title: Learning and Using Value Maps in Multi-Dimensional Choice
papers.summary:
-  We classified 538 files: 43 data, 486 code, 7 documentation, 2 materials.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 33 columns from 6 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 3 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  4 trial-level data files (E-Prime / Inquisit / jsPsych / Behaverse) were recognised. These are per-participant records of a behavioural task, so they are not listed as separate datasets. Nothing is deleted. We ran automated data-quality checks on 33 columns and found no issues.

papers.summary:
-  We classified 6 files: 4 data, 1 code, 1 documentation.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 259 columns from 4 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 259 columns; 45 columns have at least one potential issue (16 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 15 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 11 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 7 columns whose name suggests personal information; 4 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 4 columns with numeric values stored as text; 3 columns whose values look like personal information; 1 column with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 2 files are a Qualtrics survey export (20 rows look like previews/unfinished responses to review).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 53 files: 19 data, 1 documentation, 33 materials.
-  We found 19 tabular data files and extracted 212 columns from 19 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 212 columns; 94 columns have at least one potential issue (85 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 29 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 19 columns with inconsistent category casing). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 19 of 19 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Archive of OSF Storage/Data Transformations and Analyses/Preliminary Research/Extraction Document.xlsx, main folder/data/Extraction Document.xlsx, Inclusion List.xlsx, Extraction Document_Pre_Consensus.xlsx, input_effect_sizes.xlsx, crud_estimate_-Lykken.xlsx, crud_factor_-Lykken.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 781 columns; 170 columns have at least one potential issue (110 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 42 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 25 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 12 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 10 columns with numeric values stored as text; 8 columns whose values look like personal information; 6 columns with inconsistent category casing). 14 of 31 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 12 files: 2 data, 4 code, 6 documentation.
-  We found 2 tabular data files and extracted 0 columns from 2 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  2 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: overview?view_only=94136da8dfc346ddb5dbe8a15788f335: plots.RData, 2jwfk: plots.RData. We found no readable tabular data files to validate.

papers.title: The Paradox of Modern Love:  Why Romantic Signals Decline in Developed Societies
papers.summary:
-  We classified 61 files: 28 data, 18 code, 15 documentation.
-  We found 26 tabular data files and extracted 570 columns from 20 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4).
-  5 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (census_cps_table_uc1_unmarried_couples.xls: 88% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: census_cps_table_uc1_unmarried_couples.xls. We ran automated data-quality checks on 570 columns; 356 columns have at least one potential issue (349 columns with numeric values stored as text; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing; 3 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender. 11 of 11 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 1961 files: 1191 data, 400 code, 233 documentation, 24 materials, 102 output, 11 unknown.
-  We found 145 tabular data files and extracted 1595 columns from 117 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (pilot01, pilot02, pilot1, pilot20), plus 18 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  22 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (metric_registry_proposed_rows.csv: 70% of columns are free text, not variables; OCA-001_adjudication.xlsx: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; papers.title: NICE’s 2026 Consultation Draft Guideline for OCD and BDD (GID-NG10435): A Critical Appraisal with Secondary Analysis of NICE’s Published Data
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1 file: 1 data.
-  We found 1 tabular data file and extracted 108 columns from 1 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1). We ran automated data-quality checks on 108 columns; 76 columns have at least one potential issue (62 columns with numeric values stored as text; 11 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 3 columns of free text that may contain personal detail). 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Transdiagnostic factors differentially shape choices and reaction times in social evaluative learning
papers.summary:
-  We classified 47 files: 9 data, 24 code, 1 documentation, 12 materials, 1 unknown.
-  We found 8 tabular data files and extracted 139 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex19), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  4 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 R workspace file (`.RData`/`.rda`) contains no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: dataList.RData. We ran automated data-quality checks on 139 columns; 41 columns have at least one potential issue (26 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 5 columns with numeric values stored as text; 5 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 4 columns whose values look like personal information; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 2 columns that look like geographic coordinates; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long).

papers.title: Methodological Flexibility in the Iowa Gambling Task Undermines Interpretability: A Meta-method Review
papers.summary:
-  We classified 266 files: 112 data, 82 code, 66 documentation, 4 materials, 2 unknown.
-  We found 112 tabular data files and extracted 3462 columns from 79 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  27 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  4 R workspace files (`.RData`/`.rda`) contain no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: vbgeu: data/raw/multiverse/IGTdata.rdata, igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/multiverse/IGTdata.rdata, vbgeu: IGTdataSteingroever2014.zip/IGTdataSteingroever2014/IGTdata.rdata, igt-methodological-flexibility: IGTdataSteingroever2014.zip/IGTdataSteingroever2014/IGTdata.rdata.
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/metamethod review/matching of scores/scores_r2_matched.xlsx: 43% of columns are free text and 43% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset; igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/multiverse/data source.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/metamethod review/matching of scores/scores_r2_matched.xlsx, igt-methodological-flexibility: data/raw/multiverse/data source.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 3462 columns; 315 columns have at least one potential issue (88 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 76 columns with numeric values stored as text; 74 columns whose names become identical when special characters are removed; 66 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 7 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 12 survey respondents were flagged for possible careless responding. 26 of 42 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: A Meta-Analysis of Psychosocial Interventions to Improve Students’ STEM Motivation.
papers.summary:
-  We classified 90 files: 68 data, 12 code, 8 documentation, 2 materials.
-  We found 58 tabular data files and extracted 1364 columns from 54 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (overview?view_only=cee939c3d42c42b69dd2abff42092f48: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; zc9wg: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: overview?view_only=cee939c3d42c42b69dd2abff42092f48: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv, zc9wg: Data and Analysis.zip/OSF_Study1/tables/text_descriptives.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 1364 columns; 76 columns have at least one potential issue (46 columns with numeric values stored as text; 10 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 8 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 6 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 2 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic columns for Age, Race. 2 of 8 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Emotion Recognition, Face Processing and Crystallized Intelligence in Personality Pathology: A Multimethod Study
papers.summary:
-  We classified 58 files: 10 data, 20 code, 5 documentation, 6 materials, 17 output.
-  We found 10 tabular data files and extracted 842 columns from 10 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 1 collection-level file (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 842 columns; 93 columns have at least one potential issue (77 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 16 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace). 5 of 9 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Analyzing Binary Judgments: An Empirical and Simulation-Based Comparison of Aggregated and Trial-Level Approaches for Hypothesis Testing
papers.summary:
-  We classified 104 files: 66 data, 12 code, 26 documentation.
-  We found 66 tabular data files and extracted 577 columns from 64 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 4 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 tabular data file could not be read because it was not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  1 R workspace file (`.RData`/`.rda`) contains no reusable tabular data — only fitted models or saved session objects. Such files need R (and the exact packages used) to open and are not machine-readable. Share the underlying data as CSV (or a documented `.sav`/`.dta`) with a codebook so it can be reused without R: full-results.Rda. We ran automated data-quality checks on 577 columns; 52 columns have at least one potential issue (38 columns with values in a legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding; 14 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 3 columns with leading/trailing whitespace).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 810 files: 1 data, 2 code, 3 documentation, 804 materials.
-  We found 1 tabular data file and extracted 3253 columns from 1 of them.

We ran automated data-quality checks on 3253 columns; 3225 columns have at least one potential issue (3213 columns with numeric values stored as text; 11 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). We detected demographic column for Age. 1 of 1 spreadsheet file has at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 163 files: 126 data, 20 code, 17 documentation.
-  We found 98 tabular data files and extracted 4281 columns from 45 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 6 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).

papers.summary:
-  We classified 9 files: 4 data, 1 code, 4 documentation.
-  We found 4 tabular data files and extracted 35 columns from 3 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2).
-  1 file read as a table but is not a usable rectangular dataset (FINAL Themes_subthemes_codes_MH domains_RR stage 2 V2.xlsx: 50% of columns are free text and 64% are mostly empty -- this looks like a coding worksheet, not a rectangular dataset). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: FINAL Themes_subthemes_codes_MH domains_RR stage 2 V2.xlsx. We ran automated data-quality checks on 35 columns; 5 columns have at least one potential issue (2 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 1 column with inconsistent category casing; 1 column of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column with values in a legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding). 2 of 2 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Rhythm of Thought: Tracing the Dynamics of Deliberation in Reasoning
papers.summary:
-  We classified 3518 files: 2222 data, 1144 code, 6 documentation, 144 output, 2 unknown.
-  We found 58 tabular data files and extracted 990 columns from 56 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 2 study groups (ex1, ex2), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 tabular data files could not be read because they were not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  Repository https://github.com/Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought exceeds the 500 MB per-repository budget: downloaded the smallest files up to the cap, 6 files omitted. Raise `max_download_size` to include more. We ran automated data-quality checks on 990 columns; 126 columns have at least one potential issue (62 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 56 columns with inconsistent category casing; 8 columns with numeric values stored as text; 4 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 4 columns with leading/trailing whitespace; 1 column whose name suggests personal information). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender, Race. 6 of 8 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Included_Studies_References.csv, Unseen_Dataset_References.csv, core/src/main/resources/data/nlp/stop.txt, pdf-parser/src/main/resources/data/nlp/stop.txt. papers.title: Procedural learning in the serial reaction time task in individuals with and without Dyslexia: group-level and individual differences
papers.summary:
-  We classified 32 files: 28 data, 4 code.
-  We found 28 tabular data files and extracted 525 columns from 26 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex4).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (excluded_participants_study4.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; excluded_participants_study4.attention.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: excluded_participants_study4.csv, excluded_participants_study4.attention.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 525 columns; 146 columns have at least one potential issue (142 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 2 columns with inconsistent category casing; 2 columns with no observed values (entirely empty)). We detected demographic columns for Age, Gender.
